InternalAiContract.Purpose: 这是 CoronaEngine 包菜答疑使用的项目级节点积木能力与生成合同。宿主会提供用户指令、当前世界上下文、完整现有节点图和本文档；AI 只能返回完整、可见、可校验的 JSON 节点图。

Project-global node graph capability and generation contract used by Cabbage Q&A. The host sends the user instruction, current world context, complete current graph, and this file; the model may return only a complete visible JSON node graph.
InternalAiContract.SourceOfTruth: Nodes, edges, Blockly workspaces, Boolean edge conditions, global data blocks, and node x/y layout are the complete visible logic source. The model must not hide gameplay in text or code.
InternalAiContract.NoPythonFromModel: The model must not produce Python. After validation and atomic application, CoronaEngine calls nodeGraphToCode on the visible workspace and saves the compiled Python itself.
InternalAiContract.HostApplicationApi: The host validates and compiles the complete result before changing the editor. Invalid, stale, cancelled, or cross-world results leave the current project graph unchanged.

HostInputContract.UserInstruction: Natural-language request to create, extend, edit, or delete 3D game/demo/function logic. The word deno is treated as demo.
HostInputContract.ResponseLanguage: The required language for summary and newly created or renamed visible node and edge labels.
HostInputContract.RuntimeContext: Current scene and real object names, object types, object tags, available assets, audio names, checkpoints, and other project identifiers.
HostInputContract.BlockCatalog: The complete Catalog in this document. Only listed block type, field, input, output, dropdown values, and project-safe combinations may be used.
HostInputContract.ExistingGraph: The complete current project-global graph. It is the base for every operation, including create. Extend, edit, and delete must preserve unrelated graph content.
HostInputContract.ContextRule: Object names and tags used by blocks must come from RuntimeContext or already-valid ExistingGraph references. Do not invent scene bindings, actor targets, empty placeholder actors, or unnamed objects.

OperationSemantics.Operation: Build the requested playable logic in the project-global graph. Replace only when the instruction explicitly asks for a new graph; otherwise preserve useful existing logic.
Add requested states, edges, conditions, variables, and blocks while preserving all unrelated existing content.
Modify only logic identified by the instruction and preserve unrelated nodes, edges, workspaces, IDs, and layout where practical.
Remove only logic identified by the instruction, reconnect or remove affected edges safely, and keep exactly one valid start node.
Questions and explanations do not mutate the graph and must use the normal Cabbage Q&A route rather than this generation contract.
OperationSemantics.FinalWorkspaceRule: Every mutating operation returns the complete final workspace. Never return JSON Patch, diffs, partial nodes, partial Blockly fragments, or instructions for the host to finish.

ModelOutputContract.OutputRule: Return one JSON object matching ResultShape. Do not return XML, Python, a path, a file wrapper, Markdown, or explanation text outside the JSON value consumed by the host.

ForbiddenKeys.values: python sourceCode generatedCode xml filePath actorTarget sceneTarget

ModelOutputContract.IdentityRule: Copy requestId, targetId, projectScopeId, baseGraphRevision, and operation exactly from HostInput. Never calculate, rewrite, or omit them.

GenerationRules.NodeGraphRule: Return exactly one node whose nodeType is start. Other nodeType values are custom or end.
Every node, edge, and serialized block has a non-empty ID unique within its graph or workspace scope. Preserve existing IDs for unchanged content.
Every edge endpoint references an existing node and uses side left, right, or bottom with a non-negative integer index.
Every major gameplay state is reachable from start. Prefer explicit initialization, play, win, and lose states for complete demos.
Node x and y are finite numbers. Lay the main flow left-to-right with about 340 to 460 pixels horizontal spacing and at least 220 pixels vertical spacing for branches.
Node workspaces contain visible lifecycle and action blocks. Do not describe behavior only in node names or summary text.
Extend, edit, and delete preserve unrelated nodes, edges, block chains, global data, and readable layout.
GenerationRules.BlocklyRule: Use official Blockly serialization JSON under workspace.blocks.blocks.
Sequential statement blocks connect only through next.block. Never put a sibling statement block beside a chain when it is intended to execute next.
Value and statement parameters connect through inputs.NAME.block or inputs.NAME.shadow according to the Catalog input kind and check type.

For control_if, place the condition in its value input and all actions that belong to the branch under inputs.DO.block. For control_else, keep branch actions under its Catalog statement inputs such as DO or ELSE. Continue a surrounding sequence with next.block rather than nesting unrelated blocks inside the branch.
Never swallow, duplicate, or orphan blocks while editing nested control flow. Every preserved executable block must remain reachable from exactly one top-level lifecycle/event chain.
Use only block type values listed in Catalog. Use only Catalog field names, input names, dropdown option values, compatible output types, and projectUsage=project-safe blocks.
Each serialized block includes type and id. Top-level blocks include x and y for readable internal layout.
Use lifecycle hat blocks such as node_when_enter, node_while_active, and node_when_exit inside state nodes so execution timing is visible.
Use globalVariablesWorkspace only for Catalog GlobalWorkspaceRootTypes. Connect initializer and assignment values through the exact Catalog input names.

Fields and inputs are different serialization namespaces. A Catalog Field is written only under block.fields. A Catalog Input is written only under block.inputs and must contain block or shadow. Never copy an input name into fields.
control_if and control_else do not own a BOOL field. Serialize BOOL only on a nested logic_boolean block connected through inputs.CONDITION.block.

engine_rotateX, engine_rotateY, and engine_rotateZ own only the ANGLE field. Their target is inputs.OBJECT.block containing object_reference; OBJECT must never be written in the rotation block fields.
GenerationRules.EdgeConditionRule: Every edge has conditionWorkspace with exactly one visible top-level block whose output type is Boolean.
An unconditional transition uses logic_boolean with field BOOL equal to TRUE. Never represent unconditional flow with an empty conditionWorkspace.
Conditional flow uses logic_compare, logic_operation, logic_negate, input detection, collision, raycast, region, distance, variable, score, lives, or countdown Boolean combinations.
Number, text, coordinate, distance, score, and lives blocks are not valid outer conditions; connect them to a comparison block.
GenerationRules.ObjectTargetRule: Project-global object actions must identify a real scene object or tag. Prefer the Catalog object_reference output connected to OBJECT value inputs when available.
Do not leave movement, rotation, physics, collision, camera-follow, damage, spawn ownership, or deletion actions without a concrete target.
Do not serialize placeholder actor names such as object, actor, target, TODO, unknown, empty string, or arbitrary names absent from RuntimeContext.
Every statically resolvable object_reference must resolve to an exact RuntimeContext actor name. If the referenced object does not exist, the result is invalid and must be corrected before return.
GenerationRules.GameplaySafetyRule: Repeated shooting, spawning, damage, audio, or expensive raycast logic inside active loops requires a cooldown, wait, edge-trigger, or equivalent rate limit.
Variables used by win, loss, lives, score, layer, checkpoint, wave, or objective conditions must be initialized and updated on reachable paths.
Movement and camera logic must target real RuntimeContext objects and use compatible first-person, third-person, orbit, follow, or free-camera behavior.
Use collision, raycast, region, distance, ground, and tag detection blocks for 3D interactions rather than inventing unsupported physics behavior.

ProjectObjectBindingRules.Rule: The project-global graph has no implicit current actor. Every newly generated single-object action must bind a concrete RuntimeContext object through its exact NAME field or an OBJECT value input.

When a block exposes an OBJECT value input, connect object_reference. Set object_reference.OBJECT to an exact current-scene object option; use OBJECT=__manual__ with MANUAL only for a runtime-created object name that is explicitly established by reachable logic.

When a project-safe block exposes a direct NAME, PLAYER, BALL, PADDLE, CAMERA, TARGET, or similar object field instead of OBJECT, copy an exact object name from RuntimeContext or a valid runtime-created name from ExistingGraph.

Never emit empty object names, __none__, default sample names, translated object names, or placeholders such as Actor, Object, Player, Target, TODO, and unknown unless that exact name exists in RuntimeContext.

Blocks that cooperate on one controlled object, such as movement, jump, camera follow, health, collision response, and checkpoint restore, must use the same exact object binding unless the user explicitly requests different objects.
Use tags only for groups whose real tag is present in RuntimeContext or ExistingGraph. Do not replace a unique object request with a tag-wide action.

Do not introduce projectUsage=actor-context blocks into this fixed project-global graph. They require an implicit actor that this target does not provide; choose a project-safe explicit-object or tag-based alternative instead.

NodeLifecycleRootRules.Rule: For newly generated state-node logic, top-level execution roots must be node_when_enter, node_while_active, or node_when_exit. Put executable statements under the root's DO input; never leave a statement block as an orphan top-level root.
Use node_when_enter for one-time initialization, camera setup, initial placement, variable initialization, initial spawning, and audio start.
Use node_while_active for repeated input polling, movement, physics stepping, enemy updates, collision or raycast checks, cooldown checks, and other per-update gameplay.
Use node_when_exit only for cleanup, stopping temporary effects or audio, and state hand-off work that must happen once.
Generate at most one root of each lifecycle type per node. Combine actions through next.block under the same DO chain rather than creating duplicate lifecycle roots.
End nodes normally use node_when_enter for their one-time win, lose, or completion action and must not contain an unbounded active loop unless explicitly requested.
Preserve unrelated valid existing roots during edit, extend, and delete operations; normalize only the roots touched by the requested change.

EdgeConditionRules.Rule: A conditionWorkspace contains exactly one top-level Boolean output expression. It must not contain lifecycle, statement, definition, terminal, mutation, audio, spawn, delete, damage, score-update, or variable-update blocks.
Use logic_boolean TRUE for unconditional transitions. For conditional transitions, compose Boolean outputs with logic_compare, logic_operation, or logic_negate.
A numeric or string sensor output must be connected to a Boolean comparison; it cannot be the condition root by itself.

Collision conditions may use only project-safe collision blocks with an explicit subject. Because this contract target has actorBinding=none, do not introduce actor-context detect_touch, detect_touch_tag, detect_touch_started, detect_touch_tag_started, ground, or last-collision blocks.

When an explicit-context collision API is available in a future Catalog, use a started or edge-triggered condition for one-shot damage, scoring, collection, and transitions; use a continuous condition only for sustained contact behavior.
Keep side effects inside the source node lifecycle chain. The edge condition decides only whether the graph may jump.

DynamicActorRelationRules.Rule: For follow, attraction, pursuit, or other dynamic actor-to-actor movement, each requested movement axis must depend on the live coordinate of the specified source actor.
Fixed world coordinates or unrelated numeric constants do not satisfy a dynamic actor relation.
A distance condition must contain both requested actors in the same Boolean condition and must use live coordinates for the compared position.
A camera follow, orbit, or first-person block must bind NAME to the exact real actor requested by the user, independently from attraction or movement source roles.
A tag-wide operation may cover multiple targets only when RuntimeContext proves that every requested target shares that exact tag.

MacroEdgeSerializationRules.Rule: Use workspace.edges as an empty array when no macro-state transition is required.
Every source and target endpoint must use an existing nodeId, a valid side, and a non-negative integer index.
conditionWorkspace must be empty or contain exactly one visible top-level Boolean output block and must not contain side-effect statements.
When editing an existing transition, preserve its id and endpoint structure unless the requested behavior requires changing them.

ContractRepairRules.Rule: Unknown field names, unknown input names, and missing required inputs are serialization mistakes. Repair them against the exact selected block signature without inventing names.
Expand the selected contract only when the required block type or requested capability is absent from the selected contract.
During edit, preserve existing block id and type whenever the block still represents the requested behavior.
If the second result still fails schema, contract, actor binding, reachability, or requested-capability validation, reject it without applying a partial workspace.

BlockSelectionPriority.Priority: Use recommended=true and projectUsage=project-safe blocks that express the user's requested behavior directly.
For single-object WASD, jump, first-person, third-person, camera follow, or common gameplay behavior, prefer the dedicated project-safe template whose fields explicitly name the object.
For generic transforms and movement blocks with an OBJECT input, connect object_reference rather than relying on an implicit actor.
Use tag-based blocks only when the user requests a group or RuntimeContext confirms a real tag shared by multiple objects.
BlockSelectionPriority.Avoid: Do not choose projectUsage=actor-context, recommended=false legacy blocks when an equivalent project-safe explicit-object block exists.
Do not combine multiple overlapping movement systems on the same object in the same active chain unless the user explicitly requests layered control.

SafeCompositionPatterns.Pattern: In one reachable node_while_active DO chain, use object_third_person_move followed by object_arcade_jump. Bind both NAME fields to the same exact RuntimeContext object. Do not add camera, score, lives, combat, or win/lose logic unless requested.

In node_when_enter configure camera_first_person_follow for the controlled object, then in node_while_active use object_first_person_move and optional object_arcade_jump with the same object name. Use only a real obstacle tag; if no obstacle tag exists, do not invent one.

Gate mouse or key input with control_cooldown_ready or an equivalent edge trigger, perform the raycast and hit action, then consume or start the cooldown. Never fire, damage, spawn, or play audio every active update without a rate limit.
Any spawn or object-generation action reachable from node_while_active must be guarded by control_wait, control_cooldown_ready, control_start_cooldown, a one-shot input edge, or a state transition.

Initialize score, lives, floor, wave, checkpoint, or objective data on a reachable enter path, update the same variable on a reachable gameplay path, and compare that same variable in win or lose transitions.
For a feature-level request, reuse an existing reachable gameplay node when possible. Add only the lifecycle root or statement chain needed for that feature and preserve all unrelated graph content.

ThreeDDemoCompositionPatterns.Pattern: Use start for initialization, one or more custom nodes for active gameplay, and end nodes for win and lose. Give every transition a visible Boolean condition.
In node_when_enter, initialize score/lives/global data, configure camera, spawn or place objects, set physics, and start audio.
In node_while_active, run player movement, enemy behavior, collision/raycast actions, cooldown checks, scoring, life changes, recycling, and area logic.
Use object-name blocks for unique objects and tag-based blocks for groups. Names and tags must match RuntimeContext.
Combine math_random_int or math_random_float with object_set_tag_velocity_axis, object_set_random_position, object_scatter_tag, or timed state changes.
Use combat_enemy_chase_tag for pursuit, combat_enemy_contact_damage for contact attacks, and combat_melee_attack or raycast blocks for player attacks.
Choose first-person, third-person, orbit, or follow camera blocks and pair them with the corresponding movement template and input checks.
Combine velocity, gravity, impulse, collision, ground, raycast, region, and distance blocks. Use Boolean detection blocks on transition edges.
Use score, lives, countdown, cooldown, checkpoints, object counts, and variables to make explicit win, lose, wave, or objective conditions.

HostValidationPipeline.Step: Validate schemaVersion, request identity, fixed targetId, projectScopeId, baseGraphRevision, operation, workspace shape, IDs, finite positions, node types, and edge endpoints.
Validate every serialized block against Catalog type, fields, inputs, dropdown options, connection shape, and output type.
Validate exactly one start node, graph reachability, global workspace roots, and one Boolean condition block per edge.
Deserialize candidate Blockly workspaces and run validateNodeGraph and nodeGraphToCode before changing the visible graph.
Reject stale or cross-world responses, then apply atomically to the mounted project-global editor and save only after successful compilation; otherwise restore the previous graph.

GenerationScopingRules.Rule: Implement only the capabilities explicitly requested by UserInstruction. A request to add object controls is not permission to add score, lives, combat, enemies, win, lose, or unrelated states.
All examples in this contract are schema illustrations only. Never copy an example as gameplay logic.
For a small feature request, prefer the smallest valid change to ExistingGraph and preserve unrelated nodes, edges, blocks, IDs, and layout.

ResponseLanguageRules.Rule: Use HostInput responseLanguage for summary and every newly created or renamed custom node name and edge name.
Do not mix Chinese and English UI labels. Block types, field names, IDs, WASD, API names, and real RuntimeContext object names are identifiers and must not be translated.

RequestedControlPatterns.Pattern: Inside one reachable node_while_active DO statement chain, connect object_third_person_move followed by object_arcade_jump. Both NAME fields must exactly match the same real RuntimeContext object. Use object_first_person_move only when first-person control is explicitly requested.
RequestedControlPatterns.Rule: For movement templates, copy a real obstacle tag only when RuntimeContext provides one. Do not leave sample tags such as obstacle unless that exact tag exists.

Choose movement bounds that contain the current object position when RuntimeContext provides position data. Preserve existing valid bounds during edits and do not invent a narrow play area that can pin the object.
object_set_tag_velocity_axis is tag-wide axis velocity and must not substitute for single-object WASD control.
A request for controls is a minimal feature request: do not add score, lives, enemies, combat, UI, audio, win/lose states, or unrelated Demo structure.

CatalogRules.Rule: AI must preserve this Catalog and may use only listed Block type, Field name, Input name, check type, and dropdown value combinations.
projectUsage=project-safe means suitable for the unbound project graph. projectUsage=actor-context means the block expects a current actor context and should normally be avoided here.
shape=output blocks connect into value inputs or condition workspaces; shape=statement/terminal blocks connect in statement chains; shape=hat/definition blocks are top-level.
Fields with inputOwner identify the visual input row that owns the field, but serialized field values still belong in the block fields object.
